en.description: Minister Zareer officially launched the Maldives Guest Information System (MGIS) developed by MIRA. MGIS marks an important advancement in the Maldives’ tax administration and digital transformation, enabling a more streamlined and data driven approach to managing guest information. en.body: Minister Zareer officially launched the Maldives Guest Information System (MGIS) developed by MIRA. MGIS marks an important advancement in the Maldives’ tax administration and digital transformation, enabling a more streamlined and data driven approach to managing guest information. The system will also help reduce manual processes for tourism businesses in fulfilling their tax obligations.

featuredImage.alt: Finance Minister Zareer Meets Qatar National Bank CEO Abdulla Mubarak Al-Khalifa

en.title: Finance Minister Zareer Meets Qatar National Bank CEO Abdulla Mubarak Al-Khalifa
en.description: Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer met with H.E. Abdulla Mubarak Al-Khalifa, Group Chief Executive Officer of the Qatar National Bank in Doha.
en.body:
Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer met with H.E. Abdulla Mubarak Al-Khalifa, Group Chief Executive Officer of the Qatar National Bank in Doha.

The meeting focused on strengthening financial cooperation and exploring opportunities for investment and development partnerships.

Discussions also highlighted avenues to further deepen economic ties between the Maldives and Qatar in support of sustainable, long-term economic growth and development.

featuredImage.alt: Finance Minister Zareer Meets OPEC Fund President Dr. Abdulhamid Alkhalifa in Doha

en.title: Finance Minister Zareer Meets OPEC Fund President Dr. Abdulhamid Alkhalifa in Doha
en.description: Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer met with OPEC Fund President, Dr. Abdulhamid Alkhalifa on the sidelines of the 2026 Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank Annual Meeting in Doha.
en.body:
Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer met with OPEC Fund President, Dr. Abdulhamid Alkhalifa on the sidelines of the 2026 Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank Annual Meeting in Doha.

Discussions covered potential areas of collaboration under the Country Partnership Framework Agreement.

The importance of establishing an Emergency Line of Credit facility was also highlighted, alongside future engagements in high-impact areas such as water and sanitation, harbor and ports development to support sustainable development in the Maldives.

featuredImage.alt: Finance Minister Zareer Meets Kuwaiti Finance Minister in Doha

en.title: Finance Minister Zareer Meets Kuwaiti Finance Minister in Doha
en.description: Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer met with H.E. Dr. Yaqoub Al Sayed Al Rifai, Minister of Finance of the State of Kuwait, on the sidelines of the 2026 Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank Annual Meeting in Doha.
en.body:
Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer met with H.E. Dr. Yaqoub Al Sayed Al Rifai, Minister of Finance of the State of Kuwait, on the sidelines of the 2026 Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank Annual Meeting in Doha.

Discussions focused on ongoing cooperation in key sectors, including health and coastal protection, and explored avenues to further strengthen collaboration with the Government of Kuwait and the Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development through planned development projects.

featuredImage.alt: Finance Minister Zareer Speaks at AIIB Governors' Business Roundtable in Doha

en.title: Finance Minister Zareer Speaks at AIIB Governors' Business Roundtable in Doha
en.description: Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer delivered remarks at the Governors’ Business Roundtable on “Enabling Innovation: Adding Value along the Project Cycle” at the 11th AIIB Annual Meeting in Doha.
en.body:
Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer delivered remarks at the Governors’ Business Roundtable on “Enabling Innovation: Adding Value along the Project Cycle” at the 11th AIIB Annual Meeting in Doha.

Minister highlighted the need for smarter, more efficient and sustainable approaches to infrastructure delivery in the Maldives, and emphasized the importance of financing, expertise and partnerships in turning national priorities into innovative and sustainable infrastructure.

featuredImage.alt: Finance Minister Zareer Meets Qatari Finance Minister

en.title: Finance Minister Zareer Meets Qatari Finance Minister
en.description: Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises H.E. Hassan Zareer met with H.E. Ali bin Ahmed Al Kuwari, Minister of Finance of the State of Qatar, in Doha.
en.body:
Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises H.E. Hassan Zareer met with H.E. Ali bin Ahmed Al Kuwari, Minister of Finance of the State of Qatar, in Doha.

The Ministers discussed ways to further strengthen economic and trade relations between the Maldives and Qatar, including opportunities to enhance private sector development and explore new avenues for investment and economic cooperation.

The meeting also covered areas of mutual interest and opportunities to deepen collaboration in support of sustainable economic growth and development in both countries.

featuredImage.alt: Government Fully Settles and Clears $150 Million T-Bill Taken in 2019

en.title: Government Fully Settles and Clears $150 Million T-Bill Taken in 2019
en.description: The government has successfully settled the final $50 million installment of the $150 million Treasury bill facility obtained through the State Bank of India (SBI) in 2019 during former President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih’s administration, completely clearing the debt today.
en.body:
The government has successfully settled the final $50 million installment of the $150 million Treasury bill facility obtained through the State Bank of India (SBI) in 2019 during former President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih’s administration, completely clearing the debt today.

The budget-support facility was settled in sequential phases. Following this administration's payment of $50 million in January 2024 and another $50 million on May 11, 2024, today’s final payment of the remaining $50 million marks the total clearance of the entire facility.

The government assures the public that despite paying off a major portion of debt, robust arrangements are fully in place to ensure the uninterrupted import of essential commodities such as food supplies, fuel, and medical essentials, guaranteeing that foreign exchange for essential imports will not face any disruption.

According to Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA) statistics, the official reserves stood at approximately $644 million as of the end of August 2026. Therefore, claims suggesting that debt repayments would hinder the import of essential goods are entirely groundless.

In managing public debt, the government prioritizes advance planning and strategic coordination. This includes regularly depositing funds into the Sovereign Development Fund (SDF) and making necessary financial arrangements well ahead of debt maturity dates.

Furthermore, high-level discussions conducted by the government with international financial institutions and bilateral partner nations are progressing successfully. Ministry is confident that these efforts will further strengthen the nation's foreign exchange reserves.

This Ministry reiterates its firm commitment to responsible debt management, strengthening national reserves, and ensuring the uninterrupted delivery of essential services to the public.

featuredImage.alt: Finance Minister and World Bank Vice President Discuss Economic Reforms and Strategic Cooperation

en.title: Finance Minister and World Bank Vice President Discuss Economic Reforms and Strategic Cooperation
en.description: Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises H.E. Hassan Zareer and World Bank Vice President for the South Asia Region H.E. Johannes Zutt held discussions today on key economic priorities and strategic reform initiatives in the Maldives.
en.body:
Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises H.E. Hassan Zareer and World Bank Vice President for the South Asia Region H.E. Johannes Zutt held discussions today on key economic priorities and strategic reform initiatives in the Maldives.

The discussions took place during a courtesy call paid by H.E. Zutt on Minister Zareer at the ministry. The high-level meeting focused on the Government's ongoing revenue and expenditure reforms, strengthening public financial management, and identifying strategic areas for continued World Bank support.

During the meeting, Minister Zareer expressed his sincere appreciation to the World Bank for its arrangement of the Maldives' Emergency Support for Critical Services Project. This important initiative continues to play an essential role in ensuring the continuity of essential public services and logistics by maintaining critical fuel supplies across the nation.

Discussions also highlighted shared environmental priorities and long-term energy transition, including renewable energy, as well as potential areas for future support from the World Bank.

During his visit, H.E. Zutt also paid a courtesy call on H.E. President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu. Discussions with him centered on further strengthening and expanding collaboration between the Government of Maldives and the World Bank in areas of mutual interest.

The visit provided an opportunity to review ongoing areas of cooperation and explore potential avenues for expanding the World Bank’s support for the Maldives’ development priorities and strategic reforms.

featuredImage.alt: Finance Minister and SFD CEO Discuss Financing for Key Infrastructure Projects

en.title: Finance Minister and SFD CEO Discuss Financing for Key Infrastructure Projects
en.description: Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer and Chief Executive Officer of the Saudi Fund for Development (SFD), H.E. Sultan bin Abdulrahman Al-Marshad, held discussions today on potential financing opportunities for key infrastructure projects in the Maldives.
en.body:
Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer and Chief Executive Officer of the Saudi Fund for Development (SFD), H.E. Sultan bin Abdulrahman Al-Marshad, held discussions today on potential financing opportunities for key infrastructure projects in the Maldives.

The discussions took place during a courtesy call paid by H.E. Al-Marshad on Minister Zareer and focused on further strengthening the longstanding development partnership between the Maldives and SFD.

The two sides explored opportunities to secure financing for priority infrastructure projects aimed at supporting economic growth, strengthening essential public services and addressing the country's development needs.

Minister Zareer expressed his appreciation for SFD's continued support and acknowledged the Fund’s significant contribution to the Maldives' development over the past several decades.

The partnership between the Maldives and SFD dates back to 1978, when the Fund provided its first loan for the development of Male' International Airport. Since then, SFD has extended 17 development loans supporting 14 projects and programmes in the Maldives, with total financing exceeding USD 488 million.

SFD's assistance has covered several key sectors, including transport, healthcare, housing and urban development. Among its most significant contributions is approximately USD 217 million in financing for the expansion and development of Velana International Airport.

The Fund has also provided USD 50 million for the Maldives' healthcare development programme and supported major infrastructure development initiatives in Hulhumale'.

Established in 1974, the Saudi Fund for Development is the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia's principal agency for international development financing. The Fund provides concessional financing for development projects intended to promote sustainable economic and social progress in developing countries.

featuredImage.alt: Islamic Finance Integration a Government Priority: Deputy Minister Saaid

en.title: Islamic Finance Integration a Government Priority: Deputy Minister Saaid
en.description: Expanding the role of Islamic finance within the Maldives’ national financial system is a key government priority, Deputy Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Ahmed Said Mustafa has said.
en.body:
Expanding the role of Islamic finance within the Maldives’ national financial system is a key government priority, Deputy Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Ahmed Said Mustafa has said.

Speaking at the launch of the International Conference on Islamic Economics and Training Camp (IETC) 2026 on 8 September, the Deputy Minister highlighted the importance of integrating Islamic finance into the country’s broader economic framework.

He said international conferences that bring together stakeholders from different sectors play an important role in advancing this objective.

Acknowledging the support and cooperation of the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB), Said highlighted the signing of a framework agreement with the International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation (ITFC) for a new US$1.5 billion trade financing facility.

The Deputy Minister also emphasised the importance of equitable management of state resources in accordance with Islamic principles, alongside direct support for the most vulnerable members of society.

The Government of Maldives and the International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation (ITFC) have signed a new five-year Framework Agreement under which up to US$1.5 billion will be mobilised to finance public and private-sector trade operations in the Maldives.

The agreement, covering the period from 2026 to 2031, was signed at the Ministry of Finance and Public Enterprises in Malé during an official visit by ITFC Chief Executive Officer Eng. Adeeb Yousuf Al-Aama.

Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises and Islamic Development Bank Governor for the Maldives Hassan Zareer signed the agreement on behalf of the Maldivian government.

Under the framework, financing will be made available for the import and export of essential and strategic commodities. It will also cover trade financing for state-owned enterprises and eligible private-sector companies.

The agreement further provides for financing lines to be established through Maldivian financial institutions, allowing greater support to be extended to small and medium-sized enterprises and other private businesses.

In addition to financing, ITFC and the government will explore trade-related technical assistance, advisory services and initiatives aimed at strengthening trade capacity and improving access to international markets. These programmes will be aligned with the Maldives’ national development priorities.

Minister Zareer said ITFC’s support to the Maldives had expanded considerably since the institution was established, developing from assistance for the country’s energy requirements into a broader trade and development partnership.

According to the minister, the partnership now supports the import of staple foods and medical supplies while contributing to the development of important economic sectors, including fisheries and SMEs.

He highlighted the rollover trade finance facility extended to State Trading Organization PLC since 2017 as an important component of the partnership.

“This mechanism continues to provide vital liquidity support, ensuring uninterrupted bulk procurement of essential commodities and guaranteeing operational predictability for state trade,” Minister Zareer said.

He added that ITFC had remained one of the Maldives’ most dependable development partners during periods of volatility in global markets.

ITFC CEO Eng. Adeeb Al-Aama said the new framework builds on a partnership developed over several years and will expand cooperation with Maldivian financial institutions and the private sector.

“Through the agreement, ITFC will work with the government and its partners to mobilise financing for essential trade while expanding our cooperation with the private sector and financial institutions,” he said.

The latest agreement follows the first five-year Framework Agreement between ITFC and the Maldives, which was signed in 2019 and concluded in October 2024. During that period, ITFC approved US$1.7 billion and disbursed US$1.5 billion in financing to the Maldives.

Since commencing operations in 2008, ITFC has approved more than US$3.3 billion in financing for the country. The financing has supported imports of petroleum products, food commodities, medical supplies and construction materials, in addition to private-sector operations.

During his visit, Eng. Adeeb Al-Aama met President Dr Mohamed Muizzu, Minister Hassan Zareer and Maldives Monetary Authority Governor Ahmed Munawar. Discussions focused on strengthening trade finance cooperation and supporting the Maldives’ broader economic priorities.

The ITFC delegation also met representatives of STO, the corporation’s principal financing partner in the Maldives.

The delegation visited STO’s perishable and staple-food warehouse facilities in Malé and the Funadhoo Oil Terminal to review operations linked to commodities financed through ITFC facilities.

featuredImage.alt: MIB Eydhafushi branch will facilitate financial services for Baa Atoll: Minister Zareer

en.title: MIB Eydhafushi branch will facilitate financial services for Baa Atoll: Minister Zareer
en.description: Finance Minister Hassan Zareer said the opening of Maldives Islamic Bank's (MIB) new branch in Baa Eydhafushi will expand access to financial services and boost local economic activity across Baa Atoll.
en.body:
Finance Minister Hassan Zareer said the opening of Maldives Islamic Bank's (MIB) new branch in Baa Eydhafushi will expand access to financial services and boost local economic activity across Baa Atoll.

Minister Hassan Zareer stated that launching Maldives Islamic Bank's (MIB) new ATM services in Baa Atoll will expand access to financial services and boost regional economic activity.

Minister made the remarks while officiating the launch ceremony as chief guest. He noted that Sharia-compliant banking will benefit local business owners, fishermen, tourism workers, and residents, while helping small and medium enterprises (SMEs) secure financing to expand operations.

Minister emphasized that delivering equitable access to financial services nationwide remains a core pillar of President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu's administration, prioritizing full access to banking for all citizens.Pointing out that Baa Atoll is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and a major driver of national tourism, Zareer added that the new ATM facilities will directly support local tourism-related businesses and the broader economy.

He also commended MIB and other financial institutions for expanding essential banking services across the country, assuring full government support and cooperation for these initiatives.

featuredImage.alt: MIB ATM to expand financial sector in Goidhoo, boost local tourism: Minister Zareer

en.title: MIB ATM to expand financial sector in Goidhoo, boost local tourism: Minister Zareer
en.description: Minister Hassan Zareer stated that establishing a Maldives Islamic Bank (MIB) ATM in Baa Goidhoo will ease access to financial services for residents and provide significant support to the island's growing tourism economy.
en.body:
Minister Hassan Zareer stated that establishing a Maldives Islamic Bank (MIB) ATM in Baa Goidhoo will ease access to financial services for residents and provide significant support to the island's growing tourism economy.

Minister made the remarks while officially inaugurating MIB's 62nd ATM facility in the Maldives.

He noted that as the national financial sector develops, ensuring no island is left behind remains a key policy of President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu's administration. Citizens should not have to spend significant funds traveling to the atoll capital for cash deposits or withdrawals, the Minister added, emphasizing that the benefits of financial sector development must reach all citizens across the nation.

Minister thanked MIB management for expanding its services to Goidhoo and highlighted the growing public demand for Sharia-compliant financial solutions in the Maldives. The government's goal is to ensure such services are accessible across the entire country, rather than being concentrated solely in Malé and major population centers, he stated.

Pointing to Goidhoo's expanding guesthouse business and overall tourism potential, Minister added that the new ATM facility will deliver major benefits to local tourism operators and individuals looking to scale up their businesses.

He also acknowledged the ongoing efforts of MIB and other financial institutions to expand banking services nationwide, assuring full government cooperation and support for similar initiatives.

Closing his address, Minister expressed hope that the country's financial sector will continue to expand and become easily accessible to all citizens.

featuredImage.alt: MIB ATM in Kendhoo marks progress in government financial inclusion agenda: Minister Zareer

en.title: MIB ATM in Kendhoo marks progress in government financial inclusion agenda: Minister Zareer
en.description: Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer stated that establishing a Maldives Islamic Bank (MIB) ATM in Baa Kendhoo marks a major step forward in the journey to extend basic financial services to all parts of the Maldives.
en.body:
Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer stated that establishing a Maldives Islamic Bank (MIB) ATM in Baa Kendhoo marks a major step forward in the journey to extend basic financial services to all parts of the Maldives.

Speaking as the chief guest at the ATM inauguration ceremony in Kendhoo, Minister highlighted that residents can now conveniently make cash deposits and withdrawals without having to travel to another island.

Noting that the island is located in the northern part of Baa Atoll (more than 130 kilometers from Malé), Minister emphasized that geographic distance from the capital should not be a reason for disparities in the quality of services citizens receive.

Minister stated that strengthening economic activity across all islands is a key government policy, underscoring the importance of the National Financial Inclusion Strategy 2026-2030 launched by President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu in December 2025.

Minister pointed out that Sharia-compliant Islamic finance stands as one of the strategy's five key pillars, alongside expanding access to financing, broadening digital financial services, building an environmentally sustainable financial system, improving customer protection, and enhancing financial literacy.

Reflecting on the research conducted to formulate the strategy, Minister Zareer noted that despite the availability of financial services, citizens are not yet fully utilizing them. Studies reveal that 14 percent of Maldivian women and 5 percent of men remain outside the formal banking system, while only 38 percent of senior citizens utilize internet banking.

"This demonstrates that there is significant scope to increase the extent to which citizens fully utilize financial services," the Minister said.

Minister reaffirmed that the government will partner with financial institutions like MIB to boost financial literacy and empower consumers, ensuring that citizens are fully enabled to take advantage of available banking services.

featuredImage.alt: MIB ATM in Thulhaadhoo to support artisans, fishermen, and local businesses: Minister Zareer

en.title: MIB ATM in Thulhaadhoo to support artisans, fishermen, and local businesses: Minister Zareer
en.description: Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer stated that establishing a Maldives Islamic Bank (MIB) ATM in Thulhaadhoo will provide easy access to banking services, delivering major benefits to the island's artisans, fishermen, and local businesses.
en.body:
Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer stated that establishing a Maldives Islamic Bank (MIB) ATM in Thulhaadhoo will provide easy access to banking services, delivering major benefits to the island's artisans, fishermen, and local businesses.

Speaking at the official inauguration ceremony of Baa Thulhaadhoo ATM, Minister Zareer highlighted that introducing MIB's ATM services in Thulhaadhoo brings great convenience to residents, allowing them to access essential banking services without having to travel to another island.

Minister noted that Islamic banking services are becoming increasingly vital to Maldivian communities by the day, gaining substantial public support.

Minister highlighted Thulhaadhoo's historical significance as the nation's premier hub for traditional lacquer work. He noted that the skilled craftsmanship seen in items historically used in royal palaces and noble residences is still carefully preserved on the island today.

In addition, the Minister pointed out that Thulhaadhoo has a rich history in fishing, with a large portion of its population earning an income through craftsmanship and fisheries. He also noted that lacquer products crafted on the island are supplied to resorts, guesthouses, and souvenir shops across Baa Atoll.

Minister Zareer emphasized that protecting traditional craftsmanship is a crucial economic policy rather than just a cultural preservation effort. He noted that cultural heritage can only truly survive if it provides families with a viable and sustainable source of income.

Minister expressed gratitude to MIB leadership and management for expanding services to Thulhaadhoo and voiced hope that financial institutions will continue their efforts to broaden access to banking across the Maldives.

featuredImage.alt: Digital Technology Crucial for Driving Economic Growth for Small Island Developing States (SIDS) - Minister Hassan Zareer

en.title: Digital Technology Crucial for Driving Economic Growth for Small Island Developing States (SIDS) - Minister Hassan Zareer
en.description: Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hon. Hassan Zareer has emphasized that digital technology plays a vital role in driving economic growth and expanding opportunities across Small Island Developing States (SIDS).
en.body:
Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hon. Hassan Zareer has emphasized that digital technology plays a vital role in driving economic growth and expanding opportunities across Small Island Developing States (SIDS).

Speaking at the inauguration of the "SIDS Global Business Network Forum 2026 and Island Investment Forum," organized by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Minister underscored the transformative potential of modern technology for island economies.

In his remarks, Minister Zareer stated that digitalization, artificial intelligence, e-governance, fintech and other emerging technologies can help overcome barriers of distance and scale, connect communities, improve services, support businesses and create new economic opportunities.

Highlighting the practical application of technology in the Maldivian context, the Minister noted that technology is about using innovation to address practical challenges and create more efficient and connected ways of delivering services and enabling economic growth.

He also stated that governments must create the right environment through sound policies, strong institutions and clear regulations.

Reiterating the purpose of the gathering, the Minister emphasized that the forum is an opportunity not only to discuss the challenges, but to identify opportunities, share solutions, connect ideas with finance and build partnerships that can deliver meaningful results.

The SIDS Global Business Network Forum is a biennial initiative launched following the Third International Conference on Small Island Developing States in 2014. It serves as a key platform to foster private sector engagement, attract investment, and build strategic partnerships to support sustainable economic development across small island nations.

featuredImage.alt: SOEs Rightsized via Redundancy Plans - Finance Minister

en.title: SOEs Rightsized via Redundancy Plans - Finance Minister
en.description: The Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises has stated that State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) are being rightsized under a specialized redundancy framework. Responding to a question during yesterday’s parliamentary session, the Minister assured that despite the workforce reduction across…
en.body:
SOEs Being Rightsized Under Special Redundancy Plans - Finance Minister

The Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises has stated that State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) are being rightsized under a specialized redundancy framework. Responding to a question during yesterday’s parliamentary session, the Minister assured that despite the workforce reduction across state-owned enterprises, protecting the rights of all Maldivian citizens remains the government’s utmost priority.

The Minister further explained that staff reductions are being executed under established guidelines. He reaffirmed that departing employees are receiving the full redundancy packages to which they are entitled, calculated based on their length of service.

To support those seeking to establish new ventures, the Minister highlighted that a dedicated MVR 600 million fund named 'Kuvemi' has been launched through SME Digital. He further stated that both individuals affected by the SOE rightsizing process and any public sector employee looking to start a private enterprise can access financial assistance under this fund upon submitting a business proposal.

featuredImage.alt: Government of Maldives and ADB Sign USD 50 Million Energy Security Emergency Assistance Project Agreements

en.title: Government of Maldives and ADB Sign USD 50 Million Energy Security Emergency Assistance Project Agreements
en.description: The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) have signed legal agreements for the “Energy Security Emergency Assistance Project,” totaling USD 50 million.
en.body:
The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) have signed legal agreements for the “Energy Security Emergency Assistance Project,” totaling USD 50 million.

The Loan Agreement was signed by the Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises, Hon. Hassan Zareer, on behalf of the Government of Maldives. Concurrently, the Project Agreement was signed by the Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of State Trading Organization (STO), Mr. Shimad Ibrahim. Dr. Thiam Hee Ng, Regional Head of the Regional Cooperation and Integration Unit, South Asia Department, signed both agreements on behalf of the Asian Development Bank.

The primary objective of this emergency assistance project is to support the Government in responding to elevated global energy prices arising from ongoing geopolitical developments in the Middle East. The facility forms part of the Government’s efforts to secure financing from multilateral sources on concessional terms, thereby minimizing risks to the Government’s debt portfolio and supporting the achievement of its debt sustainability targets.

The Asian Development Bank continues to be an invaluable development partner to the Maldives, providing consistent and valuable support and assistance to the nation over the years.

Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer received a courtesy call from H.E. David Jessup, High Commissioner of the Commonwealth of Australia to the Republic of Maldives.

The meeting provided the opportunity to discuss key development challenges facing the Maldives, with a particular focus on advancing sustainable economic growth, economic resilience, and the country's broader development priorities. Discussions also explored opportunities to deepen bilateral economic cooperation in areas of mutual interest and enhance collaboration on initiatives that support the country's long-term development agenda.

Both sides reaffirmed the significance of the longstanding partnership between the Maldives and Australia and highlighted the importance of strengthening cooperation through continued dialogue, collaboration, and shared development objectives.

en.description: Minister Hassan Zareer attended the official launch of the Maldives Financial Expo, organised by the Maldives Monetary Authority. The Expo was inaugurated by His Excellency President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu.
en.body:
Minister Hassan Zareer attended the official launch of the Maldives Financial Expo, organised by the Maldives Monetary Authority. The Expo was inaugurated by His Excellency President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu.

The Maldives Financial Expo serves as a national platform that brings together banks, financial institutions, regulators, and key stakeholders to promote financial inclusion, enhance financial literacy, and encourage innovation across the financial ecosystem.

The event also reflects broader national efforts to build a more inclusive and resilient financial system, while encouraging public engagement and awareness on financial matters. By connecting industry players with the wider public, the expo is expected to strengthen collaboration and support the development of a more dynamic financial landscape in the Maldives.

featuredImage.alt: Minister Zareer stresses the continued institutional cooperation to strengthen economic resilience at MMA anniversary ceremony

en.title: Minister Zareer stresses the continued institutional cooperation to strengthen economic resilience at MMA anniversary ceremony
en.description: Minister Hassan Zareer graced the ceremony held to inaugurate the Maldives Financial Sector Awards and mark the 45th anniversary of the Maldives Monetary Authority, as the Chief Guest.
en.body:
Minister Zareer stresses continued institutional cooperation to strengthen economic resilience, at Maldives Financial Sector Awards Ceremony

Minister Hassan Zareer graced the ceremony held to inaugurate the Maldives Financial Sector Awards and mark the 45th anniversary of the Maldives Monetary Authority, as the Chief Guest.

Speaking at the event, Minister Zareer emphasized the importance of continued coordination between fiscal and monetary authorities, stating that cooperation between the Government, the MMA, and financial institutions is essential for strengthening economic resilience and supporting sustainable growth.

He commended the MMA for its long-standing contribution to the development of the Maldives’ financial system, highlighting its role in maintaining monetary stability and supporting national development. He also acknowledged the leadership of successive Governors and the public trust the Authority has built over 45 years.

The Minister noted progress in financial sector development, including expanded financial services and digital innovation, with the MMA playing a central role. He stressed the need for aligned fiscal and monetary policies, transparent communication, and stronger institutional cooperation.

Addressing foreign exchange challenges, Minister Zareer reiterated that improving access to foreign currency and strengthening the foreign exchange system remain key government priorities.

He further highlighted the successful repayment of the Sovereign Sukuk, describing it as the result of prudent financial management and strong institutional coordination, which has strengthened fiscal indicators and investor confidence.

The Minister concluded by welcoming the launch of the Maldives Financial Sector Awards as an important milestone for the financial sector and expressing appreciation to the MMA leadership, staff, and stakeholders for their continued service.

featuredImage.alt: Ministry Welcomes New Finance Minister

en.title: Ministry Welcomes New Finance Minister
en.description: The Ministry of Finance and Public Enterprises welcomes Mr. Hassan Zareer as the newly appointed Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises. Minister Zareer was appointed by President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu on 8 June 2026.
en.body:
The Ministry of Finance and Public Enterprises welcomes Mr. Hassan Zareer as the newly appointed Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises. Minister Zareer was appointed by President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu on 8 June 2026.

Minister Zareer has more than two decades of experience in finance, taxation, auditing, and compliance. Throughout his career, he has held several senior positions, including Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation and Commissioner General of Taxation. He also served as Director of Finance (Group Shared Financial Services) and Group Chief Compliance Officer at Villa Shipping and Trading Company Pvt. Ltd. Additionally, he served as Chairman of the Bank of Maldives from 7 March 2024 to 23 May 2024.

Senior officials and staff extended their congratulations and best wishes to Minister Zareer as he assumes leadership of the Ministry and continues efforts to strengthen public finance management, fiscal sustainability, and public enterprise reform.
The Ministry extends its best wishes to Minister Zareer in his new role.

featuredImage.alt: Finance Minister Highlights Bank of Maldives’ Strong Financial Performance and Service Delivery at Kudahuvadhoo Branch Opening

en.title: Finance Minister Highlights Bank of Maldives’ Strong Financial Performance and Service Delivery at Kudahuvadhoo Branch Opening
en.description: The Minister of Finance and Planning, Moosa Zameer, has highlighted the strong financial performance of Bank of Maldives (BML) alongside its continued expansion of banking services, during the inauguration of the Bank’s new branch in Dh. Kudahuvadhoo today.
en.body:
The Minister of Finance and Planning, Moosa Zameer, has highlighted the strong financial performance of Bank of Maldives (BML) alongside its continued expansion of banking services, during the inauguration of the Bank’s new branch in Dh. Kudahuvadhoo today.

Speaking at the ceremony, the Minister noted that the opening of the new Kudahuvadhoo branch reflects the Bank’s broader efforts to enhance financial inclusion and improve access to banking services across the Maldives. He referred to the successful completion of the nationwide ATM rollout, which has resulted in ATMs being installed in all inhabited islands, and outlined further plans to strengthen the Bank’s physical and digital presence.

The Minister stated that 2026 will be a key year for the expansion of services, with approximately 70 US dollar ATMs scheduled to be installed nationwide and 12 new branches planned to open by the end of March. He expressed confidence that these initiatives would be completed as scheduled, citing the Bank’s track record of delivering projects within agreed timelines.

In addition to service expansion, the Minister highlighted Bank of Maldives’ financial results, noting that the Bank recorded an operating profit of MVR 828 million in the fourth quarter of 2025 and achieved a profit of MVR 3.2 billion before tax for the full year. As the Government is the majority shareholder of the Bank, he welcomed the continued strong performance, stating that the results reflect both sound financial management and sustained efforts to serve the public.

The newly built Kudahuvadhoo branch replaces the Bank’s previous facility on the island and is intended to better meet the growing needs of customers in Kudahuvadhoo and neighbouring islands. The branch will provide banking services to support local economic activity, including the fishing industry and the expanding guesthouse sector, and will operate in line with Islamic finance principles. The facility is also designed as a paperless branch, with services delivered digitally to improve efficiency and customer convenience.

The Minister expressed appreciation to Mohamed Shareef, the Board, management, and employees of Bank of Maldives for their contribution to the Bank’s performance and service delivery. He acknowledged the commitment of His Excellency President Dr Mohamed Muizzu to expanding access to comprehensive financial services for the Maldivian people.

featuredImage.alt: Minister Zameer meets Oman’s Finance Minister on trade, energy cooperation and economic sectors

en.title: Minister Zameer meets Oman’s Finance Minister on trade, energy cooperation and economic sectors
en.description: Minister of Finance and Planning, Moosa Zameer, paid an official visit to the Sultanate of Oman and held an official meeting today with H.E. Sultan bin Salim bin Said Al Habsi, Minister of Finance of Oman.
en.body:
Minister of Finance and Planning, Moosa Zameer, paid an official visit to the Sultanate of Oman and held an official meeting today with H.E. Sultan bin Salim bin Said Al Habsi, Minister of Finance of Oman.

During the meeting, the two Ministers discussed ways to strengthen bilateral trade and expand economic cooperation. Discussions focused on increasing trade flows and capitalising on synergies in the maritime and fishing industries, including opportunities linked to maritime services, value chains, and related commercial activity.

The Ministers also discussed opportunities for collaboration on energy projects in the Maldives, including potential areas of partnership to support national development priorities.

The meeting reaffirmed the commitment of both countries to further enhance cooperation across other economic sectors of mutual interest.

Oman remains Maldives’ largest trading partner, primarily due to fuel imports, and the meeting highlighted the importance of maintaining and developing this longstanding economic relationship.

The Ministry of Finance and Planning will continue engagements with Oman to advance shared priorities and support stronger trade, investment and project-based cooperation.

featuredImage.alt: Minister Moosa Zameer Inaugurates Dhidhdhoo Land Reclamation for Airport and Housing Development

en.title: Minister Moosa Zameer Inaugurates Dhidhdhoo Land Reclamation for Airport and Housing Development
en.description: The Minister of Finance and Planning, Moosa Zameer, today inaugurated the commencement of land reclamation works to support the development of HA. Dhidhdhoo Airport, housing projects, and other essential services, marking a significant step in strengthening infrastructure and connectivity in the…
en.body:
The Minister of Finance and Planning, Moosa Zameer, today inaugurated the commencement of land reclamation works to support the development of HA. Dhidhdhoo Airport, housing projects, and other essential services, marking a significant step in strengthening infrastructure and connectivity in the northern Maldives.

Speaking at the ceremony held in Dhidhdhoo, the Minister said the project was focused on practical outcomes that directly improve daily life for residents. He noted that land reclamation is not only about creating additional land, but about enabling better access, stronger public services, and planned growth that benefits both Dhidhdhoo and neighbouring islands.

Highlighting the importance of the airport development, the Minister said improved air connectivity would enhance access to medical services, support travel for students and workers, strengthen local trade, and encourage investment in the region. He also underscored the importance of planned housing development to ensure safe homes, improved utilities, and orderly, liveable communities.

The Minister emphasised that essential services such as power, water, sewerage, waste management, roads, and public spaces are critical to public health, climate resilience, and overall quality of life. He outlined the government’s approach to delivering such projects through clear prioritisation, responsible financing, and a strong focus on implementation and accountability.

“As a government, we are committed to spending public funds with care and ensuring that projects deliver real results for communities,” the Minister said, adding that close coordination would be maintained with Maldives Airports Company Limited, the Dhidhdhoo Island Council, and relevant institutions to ensure timely and effective execution.

The ceremony was attended by the Member of Parliament for the Dhidhdhoo Constituency, representatives of MACL, the Dhidhdhoo Island Council, community members, and residents of the island.

Concluding his remarks, the Minister said the project forms part of a wider national effort to strengthen island communities, reduce disparities in access to services, and support sustainable development while maintaining fiscal discipline. He expressed confidence that the initiative would help Dhidhdhoo grow as a key regional hub in the north, creating opportunities, supporting livelihoods, and improving living standards for families in the area.

featuredImage.alt: Minister Highlights Fiscal Reforms and Support for Maldivian Enterprises at MSME Awards 2025

en.title: Minister Highlights Fiscal Reforms and Support for Maldivian Enterprises at MSME Awards 2025
en.description: Minister Highlights Fiscal Reforms and Support for Maldivian Enterprises at MSME Awards 2025
en.body:
Minister of Finance and Planning Moosa Zameer has said the government is working to strengthen a more conducive environment for small and medium enterprises nationwide, emphasising the central role MSMEs play in the Maldives’ economic development.

Minister Zameer delivered an address at the Maldives MSME Awards 2025 on 28 November, outlining the government’s fiscal reforms and its ongoing support for small and medium enterprises. The event, organised by the Business Centre Corporation (BCC) under the Ministry of Economic Development and Trade, recognised outstanding businesses across 24 award categories.

In his remarks, Minister Zameer emphasised the central role of MSMEs in economic growth, job creation, and national revenue, reaffirming the government’s commitment to creating a supportive environment for local enterprises. He highlighted major fiscal improvements achieved under the administration of President Dr Mohamed Muizzu, including the reduction of the fiscal deficit from 9.9 per cent of GDP in 2024 to a projected 5.5 per cent in 2025, managing expenditures within the approved budget without a supplementary budget, and maintaining a budget surplus for 40 consecutive weeks this year. He also noted the repayment of a USD 100 million sovereign bond and the growth of the Sovereign Development Fund, which surpassed USD 100 million in liquid balance for the first time.

The Minister referenced ongoing progress in renewable energy investments, increased fiscal transfers to councils, and the completion of more than 1,300 government projects through state-owned companies. He also outlined structural reforms underway, including the listing of the country’s first conventional sovereign bond on the Maldives Stock Exchange and preparations for a Sharia-compliant listing. Work continues on the Medium-Term Debt Strategy for 2026–2028, along with measures to strengthen external and domestic debt sustainability.

He underscored the government’s policy to enhance Maldivian participation in national development projects. More than 200 contractor-finance agreements valued at MVR 2.7 billion have been awarded to 53 Maldivian contractors. The Minister also reaffirmed plans to increase local involvement in the real estate and construction sectors to ensure that national development more directly benefits Maldivian workers and companies.

Highlighting targeted initiatives for MSMEs, he noted the establishment of a USD 40 million SME Impact Fund with the Islamic Development Bank Group, with the first tranche of USD 10 million now being disbursed through SDFC. Additional reforms—including revised council block grants, improved procurement processes, and upgraded digital payment systems—aim to ease administrative processes and expand economic opportunities for small enterprises.

He congratulated all winners and nominees of the MSME Awards 2025 and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to sound fiscal management and continued support for Maldivian businesses. The event concluded with the presentation of awards to outstanding enterprises from across the Maldives.

en.description: Speaking as Chief Guest at the opening ceremony of the Maldives Accountants Forum 2025 on October 11, 2025, Minister Zameer said that ongoing investment in the accounting profession is vital to building a resilient and transparent economy. The two-day forum, organised by the Institute of Chartered…
en.body:

Minister of Finance and Planning, Moosa Zameer, has reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to strengthening the accounting and auditing profession, emphasising that strong professional regulation and capability are not costs; they are enablers of prosperity and fairness.

Speaking as Chief Guest at the opening ceremony of the Maldives Accountants Forum 2025 on October 11, 2025, Minister Zameer said that ongoing investment in the accounting profession is vital to building a resilient and transparent economy. The two-day forum, organised by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of the Maldives (CA Maldives), brings together more than 300 professionals under the theme “Strengthening Financial Governance and Accountability.”

Minister Zameer highlighted that the accounting profession lies at the heart of sound public finance, resilient enterprise, investor confidence, and inclusive growth. “When accounting is strong, governance is stronger; when governance is stronger, the economy is more stable and opportunity is broader,” he said.

He noted that financial statements and audit integrity underpin revenue fairness, private sector growth, and the Maldives’ reputation among international financial institutions. “Public confidence in government revenue systems, investor trust in audited accounts, and our credibility with rating agencies are all tied to the quality and oversight of our accounting and audit ecosystem,” the Minister added.

Minister Zameer announced that the Government will provide for two priority initiatives proposed by CA Maldives in the State Budget for 2026, in collaboration with the Ministry of Finance and Planning.

The first initiative is an Audit Quality Review Programme for auditors who provide external audit services to private sector entities. This will ensure that audits are conducted in line with international standards and Maldivian regulations. “A credible quality review regime will uphold the integrity of financial reporting, safeguard lenders and investors, and strengthen confidence among international partners,” Minister Zameer stated.

The second initiative is the registration and national registry of all accountants working in the Maldives, which will improve workforce visibility, support structured professional development, and enhance compliance with evolving financial and governance standards.

“These two measures—quality review and a national registry—are practical, achievable, and mutually reinforcing. Together they will lift standards, build capacity, and create a transparent foundation for both public and private financial management,” the Minister said.

Minister Zameer underscored that the Ministry of Finance and Planning will work closely with CA Maldives to design and implement these initiatives, ensuring governance structures that maintain independence, professional integrity, and alignment with digital government efforts.

He also called on the private sector, audit firms, and professional community to actively participate in strengthening internal quality controls, mentoring young Maldivians, and embracing continuous learning through the national registry and CPD framework.

“The prosperity we seek for our people demands credible numbers, disciplined stewardship, and public trust,” Minister Zameer said. “The accounting profession is at the centre of all three. The Ministry of Finance and Planning stands ready to partner with CA Maldives and the wider professional community to strengthen financial governance and accountability across our economy.”

The Maldives Accountants Forum 2025 marks the largest annual gathering of accounting and finance professionals in the country, fostering dialogue and collaboration on governance, accountability, and professional excellence.

featuredImage.alt: Minister Zameer Highlights Partnerships as Key to Sustaining Maldives’ Tourism Success

en.title: Minister Zameer Highlights Partnerships as Key to Sustaining Maldives’ Tourism Success
en.description: Minister of Finance and Planning, Moosa Zameer, has underscored the importance of partnerships in sustaining and strengthening the Maldives’ position as a leading luxury travel destination. He was speaking as Chief Guest at the relaunch of the Experience Maldives campaign, held in collaboration…
en.body:
Minister of Finance and Planning, Moosa Zameer, has underscored the importance of partnerships in sustaining and strengthening the Maldives’ position as a leading luxury travel destination. He was speaking as Chief Guest at the relaunch of the Experience Maldives campaign, held in collaboration with Bank of Maldives (BML) and American Express, on September 27, 2025.

In his address, Minister Zameer said tourism continues to play a central role in the Maldivian economy by sustaining livelihoods, driving private investment, and supporting public services. He noted that while the Maldives is recognised globally for its natural beauty and hospitality, maintaining this success requires quality, consistency, and effective collaboration.

“Experience Maldives helps us achieve this by targeting premium travellers with compelling offers, while supporting operators across resorts, guesthouses, liveaboards, and local merchants,” the Minister said. He added that the new two-year programme would generate demand during shoulder periods, encourage longer stays, and boost ancillary spending in areas such as wellness, dining, excursions, and retail.

Highlighting BML’s long-standing partnership with American Express, Minister Zameer noted that for over two decades, the bank has been the exclusive issuer and acquirer for American Express in the Maldives. This, he said, is not only a commercial arrangement but also part of the country’s financial infrastructure, ensuring secure and reliable transactions that benefit guests, merchants, and the wider economy.

The Minister reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to working with Visit Maldives Corporation, MATI, associations, and the private sector to expand the benefits of tourism. He emphasised the need to maintain high service standards, smooth connectivity, and a strong environmental focus to retain the Maldives’ premium positioning.

“Partnerships are the engine of progress. The alignment we see tonight—between a national bank, a global payments leader, government agencies, industry associations, and businesses—is how we deliver sustainable growth,” he said.

Minister Zameer also encouraged more partners to join the Experience Maldives campaign, noting that broader participation would strengthen the Maldives’ appeal in international markets. He thanked BML and American Express for their continued commitment to supporting the tourism sector, and invited merchants across the country to take part in the opportunities the campaign presents.

The Experience Maldives campaign, first launched in 2017, is now in its fourth edition. The refreshed programme will run for two years, offering American Express Card Members exclusive privileges across a wide range of tourism and lifestyle businesses in the Maldives.

featuredImage.alt: Finance Ministry and MACL Sign Agreement for Development of Th. Vilufushi Airport

en.title: Finance Ministry and MACL Sign Agreement for Development of Th. Vilufushi Airport
en.description: The Ministry of Finance and Planning and Maldives Airports Company Limited (MACL) have signed an agreement for the development and operation of a new airport in Th. Vilufushi.
en.body:
The Ministry of Finance and Planning and Maldives Airports Company Limited (MACL) have signed an agreement for the development and operation of a new airport in Th. Vilufushi.

The agreement was signed at a ceremony held during President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu’s visit to Vilufushi on 24 September 2025. Minister of Finance and Planning, Mr. Moosa Zameer, signed on behalf of the Government, while Mr. Ibrahim Shareef Mohamed, Managing Director of MACL, signed on behalf of the company.

Under the agreement, MACL will undertake the development of Vilufushi Airport with a runway measuring 1,800 metres, alongside a passenger terminal and the full range of facilities required for an operational airport.

Speaking during the visit, President Muizzu noted that the airport is a significant infrastructure project for Thaa Atoll and confirmed that it will be completed and operational within two years and six months.

featuredImage.alt: Minister Zameer Calls for Stronger Capital Market to Support Economic Growth

en.title: Minister Zameer Calls for Stronger Capital Market to Support Economic Growth
en.description: A well-developed domestic capital market with broad participation will strengthen the Maldivian economy and enhance financial security for the public, Minister of Finance and Planning Moosa Zameer said on Wednesday.
en.body:
A well-developed domestic capital market with broad participation will strengthen the Maldivian economy and enhance financial security for the public, Minister of Finance and Planning Moosa Zameer said on Wednesday.

Speaking as the Chief Guest at the Maldives Finance Forum 2025, organised by the Maldives Pension Administration Office, the minister noted that the country’s financial system remains heavily dependent on banks despite year-on-year economic growth. He said banks alone cannot meet the financing requirements of infrastructure, trade, housing, tourism and the emerging blue economy.

The minister stressed the need to strengthen domestic revenue systems and reduce reliance on foreign aid and loans to achieve sustainable development. He added that public finance alone is insufficient to cover the costs of development projects.

The minister said a strong capital market was essential for mobilising long-term savings, broadening financing opportunities and contributing to economic growth. He called for the introduction of diverse investment products, including bonds, sukuk, and green and blue bonds aligned with sustainability goals, to improve access to finance.

He emphasised the importance of ensuring capital market access for small and medium enterprises and women-led businesses.

The minister said these objectives could only be achieved through joint efforts by the government, regulators, private companies, institutional investors and the public. The growth of the capital market must be a shared responsibility, he added.

featuredImage.alt: Signing of Grant Agreement between the Government of Maldives and JICA for the Project for Disaster Resilience Enhancement in Malé

en.title: Signing of Grant Agreement between the Government of Maldives and JICA for the Project for Disaster Resilience Enhancement in Malé
en.description: The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) have signed a Grant Agreement to support the Project for Disaster Resilience Enhancement in Malé Island (Construction Phase). The agreement, amounting to 1.56 billion Japanese Yen (approximately USD10.5…
en.body:
The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) have signed a Grant Agreement to support the Project for Disaster Resilience Enhancement in Malé Island (Construction Phase). The agreement, amounting to 1.56 billion Japanese Yen (approximately USD10.5 million) will strengthen Malé’s seawalls and provide stormwater drainage equipment to mitigate risks from waves and heavy rainfall. This Grant Agreement follows the Exchange of Notes signed on 26 July 2025 between the Governments of Japan and the Republic of Maldives. The project aims to safeguard daily life, economic activity, and community resilience by reinforcing disaster preparedness in the capital.

The Signing Ceremony was hosted by the Ministry of Finance and Planning on 09 September 2025. The Agreement was signed by the Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning, Mr. Hassan Miras, on behalf of the Government of the Republic of Maldives, and the Resident Representative of JICA Maldives Office, Mr. Taki Motoo, on behalf of JICA.

In his address, Mr. Taki highlighted that the project is a continuation of Japan’s long-standing support to the Maldives, recalling the seawall construction projects undertaken between 1988 and 2006, which protected Malé from the devastating 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami. The Resident Representative further emphasized that the new initiative will build on this legacy by upgrading seawalls and introducing specialized stormwater drainage systems to strengthen coastal protection.

Echoing this sentiment, Deputy Minister Mr. Miras in his remarks, highlighted the project as a critical step in addressing the growing threat of water-related disasters. The Deputy Minister noted that the improvements will provide vital protection for Malé’s residents, ensuring both their safety and the continued stability of the nation’s economic and social life.

The ceremony was attended by the Ambassador of Japan to the Republic of Maldives, H.E. Ms. Ishigami Rumiko, along with senior officials from the Ministry of Finance and Planning, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the Ministry of Construction, Housing and Infrastructure.

The Government of the Republic of Maldives conveys its sincere appreciation to the Government of Japan and JICA for their steadfast cooperation and continued support in advancing the country’s resilience and development.

featuredImage.alt: Minister Moosa Zameer accompanied H.E. President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu in his meeting with H.E. President Xi Jinping in Tianjin

en.title: Minister Moosa Zameer accompanied H.E. President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu in his meeting with H.E. President Xi Jinping in Tianjin
en.description: Minister Moosa Zameer accompanied H.E. President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu in his meeting with H.E. President Xi Jinping in Tianjin, where discussions centered on advancing the China-Maldives Comprehensive Strategic Cooperative Partnership (2024-28).
en.body:
Minister Moosa Zameer accompanied H.E. President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu in his meeting with H.E. President Xi Jinping in Tianjin, where discussions centered on advancing the China-Maldives Comprehensive Strategic Cooperative Partnership (2024-28).

Key areas of focus included accelerating ongoing initiatives and expanding bilateral cooperation to strengthen economic, developmental, and financial collaboration between the two nations.

This renewed commitment reinforces the long-standing ties of friendship and partnership that have underpinned Maldives–China relations for decades.

featuredImage.alt: Ministry of Finance and MACL Sign MoU for Airport and Land Reclamation in Aa. Mathiveri

en.title: Ministry of Finance and MACL Sign MoU for Airport and Land Reclamation in Aa. Mathiveri
en.description: A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) has been signed between the Ministry of Finance and Planning and Maldives Airports Company Limited (MACL) for the development of a new airport and associated land reclamation in Aa. Mathiveri.
en.body:
A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) has been signed between the Ministry of Finance and Planning and Maldives Airports Company Limited (MACL) for the development of a new airport and associated land reclamation in Aa. Mathiveri.

The MoU was signed at a ceremony held on 19 August 2025, presided over by His Excellency President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu. State Minister Hussain Imran Abdul Muhaimin signed the MoU on behalf of the Ministry of Finance and Planning, while MACL’s Managing Director and CEO, Ibrahim Shareef Mohamed, signed on behalf of the company.

This project forms part of the government’s commitment to strengthen regional connectivity and advance national development across all atolls of the Maldives.

Speaking at the ceremony, President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu emphasised that the airport to be developed in Mathiveri would create significant opportunities for the tourism industry and bring broader benefits to the local community. During his visit to Mathiveri, as part of his ongoing tour of Alif Alif Atoll, the President also announced that in addition to the airport, 26.5 hectares of land will be reclaimed to support community needs, development projects, and other public initiatives.

The President described the project as commercially viable and fully feasible, further assuring that the airport, along with the reclamation and necessary facilities, would be completed and become operational within two and a half years.

featuredImage.alt: The State Internal Audit CPD Program, an initiative by the State Internal Audit Committee, continues its mission to strengthen audit capability across the public sector

en.title: The State Internal Audit CPD Program, an initiative by the State Internal Audit Committee, continues its mission to strengthen audit capability across the public sector
en.description: Today’s session, “From Rigid to Ready: A Growth Mindset Shift for Internal Auditors”, facilitated by Ms. Reema Rasheed, Chairperson of the State Internal Audit Committee, delved into the evolving internal audit landscape and the rising expectations of the profession.
en.body:
Today’s session, “From Rigid to Ready: A Growth Mindset Shift for Internal Auditors”, facilitated by Ms. Reema Rasheed, Chairperson of the State Internal Audit Committee, delved into the evolving internal audit landscape and the rising expectations of the profession.

Through the lens of a growth mindset, participants explored how to transform challenges into opportunities, adapt with agility, and deliver greater value, gaining not only practical tools, but also a renewed perspective to embrace change as a catalyst for professional excellence.

featuredImage.alt: Finance Minister Pledges to Strengthen MIRA's Mandate and Address Key Challenges

en.title: Finance Minister Pledges to Strengthen MIRA's Mandate and Address Key Challenges
en.description: Minister of Finance and Planning, Moosa Zameer, has announced the Government's commitment to strengthening the mandate of the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority (MIRA) and addressing the challenges it faces.
en.body:
Minister of Finance and Planning, Moosa Zameer, has announced the Government's commitment to strengthening the mandate of the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority (MIRA) and addressing the challenges it faces.

The minister's assurances were delivered during his keynote address at MIRA's 15th Anniversary Celebration and "RanFanara" Awards Ceremony.

Speaking as the Chief Guest, Minister Zameer hailed MIRA as the nation's economic engine, highlighting its vital role in generating over 83% of the state's revenue. The work of every MIRA employee is directly shared in building schools, providing health services and building a brighter future for all Maldivians, he remarked.

The Minister outlined several key initiatives the Government will undertake to support the institution. He declared that finding a permanent solution to MIRA's long-standing office space shortage is a top priority. Furthermore, he revealed that significant legal reforms to enhance MIRA’s administrative capacity and independence are imminent.

Emphasizing the importance of modernization, the Minister noted that the Government's 'Maldives 2.0' policy aligns with MIRA's own Digital Transformation Roadmap, calling it an essential step to improve service quality and operational efficiency.

The ceremony also honored exemplary taxpayers with the "RanFanara" award. Minister Zameer extended his gratitude to the recipients, stating that their sincere efforts transcend legal obligations and serve as an inspiration for all citizens. He called for a cultural shift where paying taxes is viewed not as a burden, but as a fundamental civic duty.

Addressing businesses registered for the Goods and Services Tax (GST), the Minister described them as crucial partners of the state in the tax collection system and urged them to discharge their responsibilities faithfully.

Reflecting on the authority's journey, Minister Zameer described MIRA's establishment 15 years ago as a fundamental step towards building a modern, sustainable and self-sufficient economy. The Minister assured MIRA of the Government's full cooperation in achieving its goals, pledging to do everything in his power to promote and empower this vital institution.

featuredImage.alt: Maldives' Sukuk Surges as Investor Confidence Strengthens

en.title: Maldives' Sukuk Surges as Investor Confidence Strengthens
en.description: In a demonstration of strengthening investor confidence and the success of the government's fiscal management, the price of the Maldives' sovereign Sukuk has significantly increased in recent months. The Sukuk, a key indicator of the international market's faith in the Maldivian economy, was…
en.body:
In a demonstration of strengthening investor confidence and the success of the government's fiscal management, the price of the Maldives' sovereign Sukuk has significantly increased in recent months. The Sukuk, a key indicator of the international market's faith in the Maldivian economy, was trading at USD 87.44 on July 7, 2025, a significant climb from USD 64.72 in early April 2025.

This upward trajectory is a direct reflection of the government's commitment to its financial obligations and its proactive approach to strengthening the nation's economic fundamentals. A series of strategic financial manoeuvres have been instrumental in this market optimism.

In March 2025, the government successfully settled a significant repayment to a private creditor. This was promptly followed by the settlement of the Sukuk coupon payment in April 2025. These actions sent a clear and powerful signal to the global financial community of the Maldives' steadfastness in honouring its commitments, thereby bolstering investor confidence.

Furthermore, the government's commitment to fostering strong and collaborative international partnerships has yielded substantial positive results. Successful dialogues with major bilateral partners have been crucial in arranging a forthcoming refinancing package.

The surge in the Sukuk price is a clear vote of confidence from the international market, affirming the positive impact of the government's economic policies and its engagement with the global financial community. The Ministry of Finance and Planning remains dedicated to this path of prudent financial management and international cooperation.

featuredImage.alt: Maldives and Singapore Strengthen Ties with New MoU on State-Owned Enterprise Reform

en.title: Maldives and Singapore Strengthen Ties with New MoU on State-Owned Enterprise Reform
en.description: The Ministry of Finance and Planning of the Republic of Maldives has officially partnered with the Singapore Cooperation Enterprise (SCE) to boost the governance and performance of its State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs). A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed today, marking a significant step…
en.body:
The Ministry of Finance and Planning of the Republic of Maldives has officially partnered with the Singapore Cooperation Enterprise (SCE) to boost the governance and performance of its State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs). A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed today, marking a significant step in enhancing public sector efficiency in the Maldives. The agreement was formalized during the Maldives–Singapore Business Forum 2025. His Excellency Mr. Moosa Zameer, Minister of Finance and Planning, signed on behalf of the Republic of Maldives, while His Excellency Mr. Tay Lian Chew, Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Singapore Cooperation Enterprise, signed on behalf of the Republic of Singapore. The signing ceremony was held in the presence of His Excellency President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu, as part of his State Visit to Singapore.

The MoU establishes a robust framework for a strong and lasting partnership between the two parties, focused on effective and mutually beneficial cooperation. This collaboration will support the implementation of key programs in the Maldives by leveraging Singapore’s extensive public sector expertise and best practices.

The areas of collaboration will focus on the following key areas:

• Strengthening governance and institutional capacity in the management of State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs);

• Establishing robust performance monitoring and evaluation systems, including the development of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and accountability mechanisms for SOEs; and

• Enhancing financial management, operational efficiency, and the adoption of international corporate best practices within SOEs.

This MoU marks a major step in deepening Maldives–Singapore cooperation and reaffirms both nations’ commitment to good governance and public sector excellence.

en.body:
Minister of Finance and Planning, Moosa Zameer, today met with Jin Liqun, President of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), on the sidelines of the 10th Annual Meeting of the AIIB Board of Governors in Beijing, China. The meeting reaffirmed the strong partnership between the Maldives and the AIIB and explored avenues for future collaboration to support the Maldives' development agenda.

During the meeting, both parties expressed their readiness to enhance their collaborative efforts. Minister Zameer highlighted the significant ongoing projects in the Maldives that are being supported by the AIIB, including crucial assistance for the nation's recovery from the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and financing for the Waste-to-Energy program, which aims to create a more sustainable and environmentally friendly waste management system.

The Minister briefed President Jin on the comprehensive economic reforms being undertaken by the Maldivian government. He emphasized that these reforms are poised to foster robust economic growth. A key driver of this anticipated growth is the major infrastructure development currently underway, most notably the new terminal at Velana International Airport and the establishment of new airports in various regions, which are expected to boost the tourism sector and overall economic activity.

Discussions also centered on the future financing needs of the Maldives. Minister Zameer elaborated on the government's vision for national development and identified key areas where the AIIB's support would be instrumental in achieving these goals

Minister Zameer, who is also the Governor of the AIIB for the Maldives, was accompanied by Dr. Fazeel Najeeb, Ambassador of the Maldives to China; Ali Sajid Shakir, Second Secretary at the Embassy of Maldives in China; Mizna Waheed, Second Secretary at the Embassy of Maldives in China; and, Rauha Ibrahim, Resource Mobilization Analyst, Ministry of Finance and Planning.

In addition to President Jin Liqun, AIIB delegation included Rajat Misra, Acting Chief Investment Officer, and Managers Hari Bhaskar and Toshiaki Keicho.
